name: Saint Cyril of Alexandria
history: Patriarch of Alexandria for over thirty years and one of the great theologians of the Incarnation. When Nestorius of Constantinople taught that Mary should not be called Mother of God, Cyril defended the truth that Christ is one divine Person, and presided at the Council of Ephesus in 431, which upheld the title Theotokos. Leo XIII named him a Doctor of the Church.
life: Cyril succeeded his uncle Theophilus as patriarch of Alexandria in 412. His early years were marked by fierce conflict in a turbulent city, and his methods were sometimes harsh; the Church honours him for his teaching and his holiness, not for every act of his life. From 428 he gave himself to the question raised by Nestorius. If Mary is only the mother of the man Jesus, Cyril argued, then the one who was born, suffered and died for us is not truly God, and we are not saved. He wrote to Nestorius, to Rome and to the emperor, and Pope Celestine entrusted him with the case. At Ephesus in 431 the council deposed Nestorius and proclaimed Mary Mother of God, to the joy of the people. In 433 Cyril reached agreement with the bishops of Antioch, who had opposed him. His commentaries on Scripture are still read.
prayerTo: Saint Cyril, you fought for the truth that the Child of Mary is God made man. Pray for theologians and teachers, that they may serve the faith humbly and well. Pray for me, that I may honour Mary as Mother of God, worship her Son in spirit and truth, and defend the faith with charity as well as zeal. Amen.
penance: Pray the Hail Mary slowly ten times today, dwelling each time on the words Mother of God, and make amends for one hard word you have spoken to another.
meditation: Cyril saw that everything depends on who Christ is. If someone asked you today who Jesus is, what would you say?
prayer: O God, Who made Cyril, Your Confessor and Bishop, an unconquerable champion of the most Blessed Virgin Mary’s divine motherhood, grant that we who believe that she is truly the Mother of God may be saved by her motherly protection. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
